heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Algeria
heroData.subtitle: Global Employment Solution for 2025
heroData.description: Hire employees in Algeria legally without a local entity. Our EOR partners handle payroll, taxes, and compliance while you manage the work.
heroData.bestFor: International companies expanding to North Africa

sections.title: Onboarding Process via EOR in Algeria
sections.subtitle: Timeline: 1-2 weeks

steps.title: Contract Drafting and Approval
steps.description: The EOR drafts a locally compliant employment contract in Arabic and French. It must include core elements like salary in DZD, job description, 40-hour work week, and statutory benefits according to the Algerian Labor Code.

steps.title: Document Collection and Verification
steps.description: Employee provides proof of identity (National ID/Passport), proof of residence, social security number (CNAS), and educational certificates. For foreign employees, work permit applications are initiated at this stage.

steps.title: Social Security Registration (CNAS)
steps.description: The EOR registers the new hire with the Caisse Nationale des Assurances Sociales (CNAS). This is mandatory for all private sector employees to ensure health and retirement coverage.

steps.title: Medical Examination
steps.description: By law, the employee must undergo a medical check-up (Médecine du Travail) to ensure fitness for the role. The EOR schedules this with a local authorized physician.

steps.title: IT and Resource Allocation
steps.description: Equipment is shipped to the employee. The EOR manages the logistics of delivering laptops and devices while ensuring all local tax implications for 'benefits in kind' are accounted for.

items.title: Fixed-Term vs Permanent Contracts
items.text: Permanent (CDI) is the norm. Fixed-term (CDD) is only allowed for specific temporary tasks. Misclassification leads to heavy fines and automatic conversion to permanent status.

items.title: Minimum Wage 2025
items.text: The National Minimum Guaranteed Salary (SNMG) is 20,000 DZD per month. Competitive salaries for international roles typically range from 80,000 to 250,000 DZD.

items.title: Employer Liability Limit
items.text: Using an EOR shifts the legal liability of the 'Employer' to the local entity provider, protecting your parent company from direct litigation in Algerian labor courts.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle the annual 30-day leave?
faqs.answer: Yes, the EOR tracks and manages the statutory 30 calendar days of paid annual leave. They ensure the holiday pay is calculated correctly based on the 'reference period' (July 1 to June 30).

faqs.question: Can I hire expats through an Algerian EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it requires a work permit (Autorisation de travail) and a residence card. The EOR must prove that no local candidate could fill the role (National Preference).

faqs.question: What is the notice period for termination?
faqs.answer: It varies by seniority but is typically 1 month for junior staff and up to 3-6 months for senior executives, as defined in the contract and collective agreements.

items.title: Ramadan Scheduling
items.text: During Ramadan, working hours are reduced by law. Most offices operate from 9:00 AM to 3:30 or 4:00 PM. Expect slower processing for administrative tasks.

items.title: Transportation Allowance
items.text: It is standard practice to provide a transportation allowance (Indemnité de Transport) as part of the monthly compensation package, which is partially tax-exempt.

items.title: Thirteenth Month Bonus
items.text: While not legally mandatory, a 13th-month bonus or performance incentive is widely expected at the end of the calendar year to attract top talent.

items.title: Local Support Hours
items.text: Our Algerian desk operates Sunday to Thursday, 09:00 to 17:00 (GMT+1), following the standard local work week.

items.title: Multilingual Communication
items.text: All service delivery can be conducted in English, French, or Arabic depending on your preference and regional team needs.

steps.title: Data Gathering & Reconciliation
steps.description: Collect gross salary details, overtime hours, bonuses (PRI/PRC), and deduction updates. Reconcile against the previous month to ensure zero discrepancies.

steps.title: Social Security (CNAS) Calculation
steps.description: Calculate the 9% employee deduction and the 26% employer contribution. These must be declared monthly via the DAS portal.

steps.title: Income Tax (IRG) Withholding
steps.description: Apply the progressive IRG (Impôt sur le Revenu Global) tax brackets to the net taxable income. Rates range from 0% to 35% depending on the salary level.

steps.title: Net Pay Distribution
steps.description: Funds are dispersed to employee bank accounts via local bank transfers. Payslips (Bulletin de Paie) are generated in French/Arabic and distributed digitally or physically.

steps.title: Statutory Reporting & Filing
steps.description: File the monthly G50 tax form and social security declarations. Ensure payments are made by the 15th (G50) and 20th (CNAS) of the following month to avoid late fees.

items.title: G50 Late Filing Penalties
items.text: Failure to file the G50 form and pay IRG by the 15th of the month results in a 10% penalty plus 3% per month of delay. Strict adherence is required.

items.title: Tax Exempt Allowances
items.text: Certain allowances like family allowances (Allocations Familiales) and a portion of transport/meal allowances are exempt from CNAS and IRG.

items.title: Bank Transfer Timing
items.text: Local bank transfers between different Algerian banks can take 2-4 business days. Plan the payroll run at least 5 days before the month-end.

faqs.question: Are payslips required in a specific language?
faqs.answer: Yes, payslips are typically prepared in French, but having an Arabic version is recommended for full legal compliance and clarity for all employees.

faqs.question: What is the maximum overtime allowance?
faqs.answer: Overtime is capped at 20% of the normal legal duration (8 hours per week). All overtime must be paid with a premium of at least 50% above the base hourly rate.

faqs.question: How are severance payments handled?
faqs.answer: Severance is calculated based on years of service. It is generally tax-exempt up to certain limits defined by the annual Finance Law.

rows.label: CNAS Social Security
values: 9% contribution for health, pension, and life insurance.

rows.label: Progressive IRG
values: Withheld at source based on taxable income.

rows.label: Mutual Insurance
values: Optional top-up health insurance common in multinationals.

rows.label: Union Dues
values: Deducted only upon written request from the employee.

steps.title: Base Salary Identification
steps.description: Defining the monthly base gross salary before any specific job allowances.

steps.title: CNAS Deduction (9%)
steps.description: Calculating the mandatory employee social insurance deduction on the full gross amount.

steps.title: Taxable Income Determination
steps.description: Calculating the Net Taxable Salary (Gross - 9% CNAS). This is the base for IRG.

steps.title: IRG Bracket Application
steps.description: Applying the progressive IRG tax rates (up to 35%) based on the latest 2025 Finance Law bands.

steps.title: Net Take-Home Sum
steps.description: Adding back specific non-taxable allowances (like family or travel) to arrive at the final amount paid into the bank.

items.title: Tax Free Threshold
items.text: Salaries below 30,000 DZD per month are entirely exempt from IRG (Income Tax).

items.title: Total Employer Burden
items.text: Employers must budget for an additional 26% on top of the gross salary for their share of CNAS contributions.

items.title: Sector-Specific Levies
items.text: Construction and public works (BTPH) have higher payroll costs due to the mandatory CACOBATPH vacation fund.

faqs.question: Does it calculate 'Total Cost to Hire'?
faqs.answer: Yes, our calculator displays both the employee's net and the employer's total cost inclusive of all payroll taxes.

faqs.question: Is the 13th month factor included?
faqs.answer: Users can toggle the 'Annual Bonus' field to see the impact on effective monthly take-home pay.

faqs.question: How often is the IRG logic updated?
faqs.answer: The calculator is updated annually in January to reflect the changes in the Official Gazette (Journal Officiel).

items.title: Marital Status
items.text: IRG tax can vary slightly based on marital status and number of children; our calculator uses the standard 'Single' status by default.

items.title: South Zone Abatements
items.text: Employees working in the Saharan regions (Hassi Messaoud, etc.) are entitled to significant IRG reductions (up to 50%).

items.title: Disability Credits
items.text: Employees with recognized disabilities have different tax exemption thresholds which should be applied manually.

heroData.title: Incorporation & Entity Setup in Algeria
heroData.subtitle: Legal Entity Formation for 2025
heroData.description: Establish your business in Algeria with full legal compliance. We guide you through the choosing the right entity type, navigating the 51/49 rule, and securing all local permits.
heroData.bestFor: Foreign investors and companies seeking a permanent local presence

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Obtain a 'Dénomination' certificate from the Centre National du Registre du Commerce (CNRC) to reserve the company name.

steps.title: Notarial Act
steps.description: Drafting and signing the Articles of Association (Statutes) before an Algerian Public Notary. This is a mandatory formal step.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Deposit the minimum share capital into a local 'blocked' bank account. For a SARL, the minimum is typically 100,000 DZD.

steps.title: Registration with CNRC
steps.description: Submitting the full dossier to the CNRC to receive the Commercial Registry card (RC).

steps.title: Tax & Social Security ID
steps.description: Obtaining the NIF (Tax ID) and NIS (Statistical ID), and registering with CASNOS/CNAS for employer contributions.

items.title: SARL (LLC)
items.text: The most common form for small to medium businesses. Requires at least 2 partners and has a low minimum capital requirement.

items.title: EURL (Single-Member LLC)
items.text: Ideal for solo entrepreneurs. It offers the same limited liability benefits as a SARL but with only one shareholder.

items.title: The 51/49 Rule
items.text: While largely abolished for general trade, the 51/49 rule (requiring majority local ownership) still applies to 'strategic' sectors like hydrocarbons and large-scale retail.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner be the General Manager (Gérant)?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they must obtain a residence card (Carte de Résident) and a work permit if they are based in Algeria.

faqs.question: Is a physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes. You must provide a commercial lease agreement (Bail Commercial) or a domiciliation contract to register with the CNRC.

faqs.question: How long does it take to open a bank account?
faqs.answer: Once the RC card is obtained, opening a full operational account takes 1-2 weeks, depending on the bank's KYC process.

items.title: Apostilled Documents
items.text: All parent company documents (for subsidiaries) must be translated and legalized or apostilled by the Algerian embassy.

items.title: Criminal Record Check
items.text: Foreign managers must provide a clean criminal record (Casier Judiciaire) from their home country.

items.title: Sector-Specific Licenses
items.text: Identify if your activity (e.g., pharmaceuticals, transport) requires prior technical approval before the CNRC filing.

items.title: Multilingual Communication

items.title: IFRS Alignment
items.text: The Algerian SCF is heavily inspired by IAS/IFRS standards, making it easier for multinational corporations to consolidate their Algerian accounts with global reports.

items.title: Mandatory Arabic/French Posting
items.text: By law, accounting journals and mandatory registers must be kept in Arabic or French. Digital records must be exportable in forms readable by tax authorities.

items.title: Certified Accountant Requirement
items.text: Financial statements must be certified by a member of the National Chamber of Accountants (ONEC) to be valid for tax and banking purposes.

steps.title: Monthly Bookkeeping & G50

steps.title: Quarterly Reconciliations

steps.title: Inventory & Year-End Closing

steps.title: Legal Inventory Book Completion
steps.description: The legal 'Livre d'Inventaire' and 'Livre Journal' must be completed and paraf'd (stamped) by the local court or notary.

steps.title: Financial Statement Submission
steps.description: Submit the annual tax return (Liasse Fiscale) to the DGE or local CDI by April 30th of the following year.

faqs.question: Can I use QuickBooks or Xero in Algeria?
faqs.answer: Yes for internal management, but those tools often lack the specific Algerian tax reports (G50, 301bis) and SCF chart of accounts.

faqs.question: What is the retention period for accounting documents?
faqs.answer: By law, all accounting records, original invoices, and bank statements must be stored for a minimum of 10 years.

faqs.question: Is E-invoicing mandatory in Algeria?
faqs.answer: Paper-based invoices with original stamps are still the legal default. E-invoicing pilots are expected through 2025/2026.

items.title: Original Documents
items.text: Scanning is useful, but the tax inspectorate (Direction des Grandes Entreprises) always requires original stamped paper invoices during audits.

items.title: NIF Requirement
items.text: Every invoice received from a local supplier must contain your company's unique Tax Identification Number (NIF) to be deductible.

items.title: Bank Reconciliation

items.title: Board Resolution Rigor

items.text: Algeria has treaties with over 50 countries, including France, UAE, and the UK, which can reduce withholding tax rates for international service contracts.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late G50 filing?
faqs.answer: The initial penalty is 10% of the tax due, with an additional 3% for each month of delay.

faqs.question: Can I claim VAT back on fuel?
faqs.answer: No, VAT on fuel for business vehicles is generally not deductible under Algerian law.

faqs.question: Is there a tax on staff training?
faqs.answer: Yes, companies with >20 staff must spend 1% of the wage bill on training or pay it as a tax to the treasury.
